title: Beef Wellington
intro: A whole beef fillet wrapped in mushroom duxelles, prosciutto and golden puff pastry, carved to reveal a rosy centre.
ingredients: 1 kg (2¼ lb) centre-cut beef fillet, trimmed
500 g (1 lb 2 oz) all-butter puff pastry
2 egg yolks, beaten with 1 tsp water
Flaky sea salt and black pepper
steps: Pat the fillet dry and season it generously all over. Heat the oil in a heavy frying pan until it just starts to smoke, then sear the beef for about 1 minute on each side and on both ends so the whole surface is deep brown. Lift it onto a board, brush it all over with the mustard while still warm and leave to cool.

Pulse the mushrooms in a food processor until they look like coarse crumbs. Melt the butter in the same pan over medium-high heat, add the shallots and garlic for 2 minutes, then add the mushrooms and thyme. Cook, stirring often, for 12 to 15 minutes until every drop of moisture has evaporated and the mixture is dry and dark. Season and leave to cool completely.

Lay a large sheet of cling film on the worktop and arrange the prosciutto slices on it in an overlapping rectangle wide enough to wrap the fillet. Spread the cooled mushroom mixture evenly over the prosciutto.
Set the beef at one edge and use the cling film to roll the prosciutto and mushrooms tightly around it, twisting the ends like a sweet wrapper. Chill for at least 30 minutes so it holds its shape.

Roll the pastry out on a lightly floured surface to a rectangle about 3 mm (⅛ in) thick and large enough to enclose the beef. Unwrap the fillet, set it in the centre and brush the pastry edges with egg yolk. Fold the pastry over, trim the excess, press the seams to seal and turn the parcel seam-side down. Brush all over with egg yolk, score a light pattern with the back of a knife and chill for another 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F, fan 180 °C). Place the Wellington on a baking sheet lined with parchment, brush with egg once more and sprinkle with flaky salt.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the pastry is deeply golden and a probe in the centre reads 50 °C (122 °F) for medium-rare. Rest on the tray for 10 minutes before carving into thick slices.

title: Ribeye Steak
intro: A thick, well-marbled ribeye seared in a screaming-hot pan and basted with foaming garlic and thyme butter.
ingredients: 2 bone-in or boneless ribeye steaks, about 350 g (12 oz) each and 3 to 4 cm (1½ in) thick
1 tbsp neutral oil with a high smoke point
steps: Take the steaks out of the fridge 30 to 40 minutes before cooking and pat them very dry with kitchen paper. Season both sides heavily with salt and pepper.
Set a heavy cast-iron or stainless pan over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes until it is very hot. Add the oil and swirl to coat.
Lay the steaks in the pan away from you and leave them alone for 3 minutes so a dark crust forms. Flip and cook for another 3 minutes on the second side.
Turn the heat down to medium. Add the butter, garlic and herbs to the pan; once the butter foams, tilt the pan and spoon it over the steaks continuously for 1 to 2 minutes, flipping once more.
Check with a probe thermometer: pull the steaks at 52 °C (125 °F) for medium-rare or 57 °C (135 °F) for medium. Thicker steaks may need an extra minute or two per side.
Transfer the steaks to a warm plate, spoon the pan butter over the top and rest for 8 to 10 minutes before slicing against the grain.

title: Bulgogi
intro: Paper-thin slices of beef soaked in a sweet soy, pear and sesame marinade, then flash-cooked over fierce heat.
ingredients: 700 g (1½ lb) beef sirloin or ribeye, sliced paper-thin against the grain
½ Asian pear (or 1 small sweet apple), peeled and grated
4 spring onions, cut into 4 cm lengths
Steamed short-grain rice and lettuce leaves, to serve
steps: If slicing the beef yourself, freeze it for 30 minutes first so you can cut it very thinly with a sharp knife.
In a large bowl, stir together the grated pear, soy sauce, brown sugar, honey, sesame oil, garlic, ginger and pepper until the sugar dissolves.
Add the beef, onion, carrot and spring onions and mix with your hands so every slice is coated. Cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 1 hour, or up to overnight.

Heat a wide cast-iron pan, griddle or barbecue grate until very hot and brush with the vegetable oil. Cook the beef in small batches in a single layer for 1 to 2 minutes per side, letting the edges caramelise without crowding the pan.
Return all the beef to the pan for a final 30 seconds to warm through, then pile onto a platter and scatter with sesame seeds.
Serve immediately with steamed rice and lettuce leaves for wrapping.

title: Pot Roast
intro: A whole chuck roast cooked slowly with wine, stock and root vegetables until it falls apart under a fork.
ingredients: 1.8 kg (4 lb) boneless beef chuck roast
4 large carrots, cut into 5 cm chunks
700 g (1½ lb) small waxy potatoes, halved
steps: Heat the oven to 160 °C (325 °F, fan 140 °C). Pat the beef dry and season it well with salt and pepper on all sides.
Warm the oil in a large, heavy casserole dish with a lid over medium-high heat. Brown the beef for 4 to 5 minutes per side until it has a deep crust all over, then move it to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium, add the onions and cook for 5 minutes until softened and golden at the edges. Stir in the garlic and tomato purée and cook for 1 minute more.
Pour in the wine and let it bubble for 2 to 3 minutes, scraping up the browned bits from the bottom. Add the stock, bay leaves, thyme and rosemary and bring to a simmer.
Return the beef to the pot along with any juices. Cover and transfer to the oven for 2 hours.
Tuck the carrots, potatoes and celery around the beef, replace the lid and cook for another 1 to 1½ hours, until the vegetables are tender and the meat pulls apart easily.
Lift the beef and vegetables onto a platter and keep warm. Skim the fat from the cooking liquid, simmer it on the hob for 5 to 10 minutes to reduce slightly, season, and spoon over the meat to serve.

title: Black Forest Cake
intro: Layers of light chocolate sponge soaked in kirsch, filled with whipped cream and sour cherries and finished with chocolate shavings.
ingredients: 60 g (¼ cup) unsalted butter, melted and cooled
680 g (24 oz) jar sour cherries in syrup, drained with syrup reserved
2 tbsp caster sugar, for the cherry filling
750 ml (3 cups) double or whipping cream, cold
100 g (3½ oz) dark chocolate, for shaving
12 fresh or maraschino cherries, to decorate
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F, fan 160 °C). Grease two 20 cm (8 in) round tins and line the bases with parchment.

Whisk the eggs, 180 g sugar and vanilla with an electric mixer on high speed for 8 to 10 minutes until pale, thick and tripled in volume. Sift the flour and cocoa over the top in two additions, folding gently with a large spoon each time so you keep the air in.

Pour the melted butter down the side of the bowl and fold it in with a few strokes. Divide between the tins and bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the sponges spring back when pressed. Cool in the tins for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a rack.

Make the cherry filling: set aside 12 cherries for the top. Whisk the cornflour and 2 tbsp sugar into 250 ml (1 cup) of the reserved syrup in a small pan and cook over medium heat, stirring, for 3 to 4 minutes until thick and glossy. Stir in the remaining cherries and 2 tbsp of the kirsch and let cool completely.
Whip the cold cream with the icing sugar to firm peaks. Split each cooled sponge in half horizontally to give four layers and brush each cut side with the remaining kirsch.

Place one layer on a serving plate, spread with a thin layer of cream, then half the cherry filling. Top with a second sponge, a thicker layer of cream, then a third sponge, the rest of the cherries and more cream. Finish with the last sponge.
Cover the top and sides with the remaining cream. Run a vegetable peeler along the chocolate bar to make curls and press them around the sides and over the top; arrange the reserved cherries on top.
Chill for at least 1 hour, or ideally 4, so the layers settle before slicing.

title: Matcha Mille Crêpe Cake
intro: Twenty delicate green-tea crêpes stacked with lightly sweetened matcha cream into a cake that needs no oven.
ingredients: 60 g (¼ cup) unsalted butter, melted, plus extra for the pan
600 ml (2½ cups) double or whipping cream, cold
steps: Whisk the eggs and caster sugar in a large bowl until smooth. Sift in the flour, 2 tablespoons of the matcha and the salt and whisk to a thick paste, then gradually whisk in the milk, melted butter and vanilla until the batter is thin and lump-free. Strain through a fine sieve, cover and rest in the fridge for at least 30 minutes.
Heat a 20 cm (8 in) non-stick frying pan over medium heat and brush lightly with butter. Pour in about 60 ml (¼ cup) of batter, swirling immediately so it coats the base in a thin, even layer.

Cook for 60 to 90 seconds until the edges lift and the surface looks dry, flip and cook for 15 seconds more. Slide onto a plate and repeat, stacking the crêpes with no paper between them, until you have 20 to 22. Let them cool completely.
Sift the remaining tablespoon of matcha with the icing sugar into the cold cream and whip to soft but spreadable peaks.

Set the first crêpe on a flat serving plate and spread with a thin, even layer of cream, leaving a 5 mm border. Top with the next crêpe and repeat, pressing each one lightly so the stack stays level, finishing with a bare crêpe on top.
Cover loosely and chill for at least 2 hours so the layers firm up. Dust generously with matcha just before slicing with a long, sharp knife wiped between cuts.

title: Grilled Chicken and Rice Bowl
intro: A meal-prep staple built around a generous portion of smoky grilled chicken breast over jasmine rice with charred peppers and lime.
ingredients: 800 g (1¾ lb) skinless chicken breast, about 200 g (7 oz) per person
300 g (1½ cups) uncooked jasmine or basmati rice
steps: Slice each chicken breast horizontally so you have thinner, even pieces. Toss with 1 tablespoon of the oil, the lime zest, half the lime juice, garlic, paprika, cumin, oregano and a good pinch of salt. Leave for 15 minutes while you cook the rice.

Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then cook it in 450 ml (scant 2 cups) water: bring to the boil, cover, reduce to the lowest heat for 12 minutes, then rest off the heat for 10 minutes before fluffing.
Heat a griddle pan or barbecue to high. Toss the peppers and onion with the remaining oil and grill for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until charred and tender. Set aside.
Grill the chicken for 4 to 5 minutes per side until well marked and cooked through, or until a probe reads 74 °C (165 °F). Rest for 5 minutes, then slice.
Divide the rice between four bowls and top each with 200 g of chicken, a quarter of the grilled vegetables and the cherry tomatoes.
Squeeze over the remaining lime juice, season and finish with coriander. Each bowl provides roughly 550 kcal and 52 g protein.

title: Baked Salmon with Quinoa and Greens
intro: Lemon-roasted salmon fillets on a bed of fluffy quinoa with garlicky wilted spinach and roasted broccoli.
ingredients: 2 skinless salmon fillets, about 180 g (6½ oz) each
250 ml (1 cup) water or light stock
200 g (7 oz) broccoli, cut into small florets
1 lemon, half sliced and half juiced
1 tsp dried dill or 2 tbsp fresh dill
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F, fan 180 °C) and line a baking tray with parchment.

Rinse the quinoa in a sieve, tip it into a small pan with the water and a pinch of salt and bring to the boil. Cover, simmer gently for 15 minutes until the water is absorbed, then rest off the heat for 5 minutes and fluff with a fork.

Spread the broccoli on one side of the tray, toss with half the oil and season. Set the salmon on the other side, season, lay the lemon slices on top and scatter with dill. Roast for 12 to 14 minutes until the salmon flakes easily and the broccoli is charred at the edges.
Meanwhile, warm the remaining oil in a large pan over medium heat, add the garlic for 30 seconds, then add the spinach in handfuls and toss for 1 to 2 minutes until just wilted. Season.
Divide the quinoa between two bowls, add the spinach and broccoli and set a salmon fillet on top.
Squeeze the lemon juice over everything before serving. Each bowl comes to about 580 kcal with 46 g protein.

title: Lean Turkey Chili
intro: A thick, smoky chili made with lean turkey mince and two kinds of beans that gets better the day after.
ingredients: 800 g (1¾ lb) lean turkey mince (93% or leaner)
400 g (14 oz) tin kidney beans, drained and rinsed
400 g (14 oz) tin black beans, drained and rinsed
Chopped coriander and sliced spring onions, to serve
steps: Warm the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the turkey and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it up with a spoon, until no pink remains and it starts to brown.
Add the onion and pepper and cook for 5 minutes until softened, then stir in the garlic, chili powder, cumin, paprika and oregano and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the chopped tomatoes, tomato purée, both tins of beans and the stock. Season with salt and pepper and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low, partially cover and simmer for 30 to 35 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and rich. Add a splash of water if it gets too dry.
Taste and adjust the seasoning, then ladle into bowls and top with coriander and spring onions. A quarter of the pot gives roughly 520 kcal and 54 g protein.

title: Egg White and Cottage Cheese Omelette
intro: A fluffy, oversized omelette loaded with mushrooms, spinach and creamy cottage cheese that packs in protein without much fat.
ingredients: 250 ml (1 cup) liquid egg whites, about 7 egg whites
steps: Whisk the egg whites and whole egg with a pinch of salt and pepper until just combined and slightly frothy.

Heat the oil in a 24 cm (9½ in) non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the mushrooms for 4 minutes until golden, add the spring onions and spinach and cook for 1 minute more until the leaves wilt. Tip onto a plate.

Return the pan to medium heat, pour in the egg mixture and tilt the pan to cover the base. As the edges set, draw them towards the centre with a spatula and let the raw egg run underneath, for about 2 to 3 minutes.
When the top is almost set but still glossy, spoon the cottage cheese and the vegetables over one half and sprinkle with herbs. Fold the other half over and cook for 1 minute more.
Slide onto a plate and serve with the toast. The whole plate comes to about 480 kcal with 54 g protein.

title: Greek Yogurt Protein Bowl
intro: Thick Greek yogurt whipped with vanilla protein powder and topped with oats, berries and crunchy almonds for a five-minute breakfast.
ingredients: 30 g (1 scoop) vanilla whey or plant protein powder
2 to 3 tbsp milk or water, as needed
100 g (¾ cup) mixed berries, fresh or frozen and thawed
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl and sift the protein powder over it. Stir vigorously, adding a splash of milk or water at a time, until it is completely smooth with no dry lumps.
Toast the oats in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes until they smell nutty, or leave them raw for a softer texture.
Scatter the oats and berries over the yogurt, then add the almonds.
Drizzle with honey, dust with cinnamon and eat straight away. The bowl delivers about 560 kcal and 61 g protein.

title: Seared Tuna Steak with Edamame
intro: Sesame-crusted tuna steaks seared rare and served over warm edamame with a sharp ginger-soy dressing.
ingredients: 2 fresh tuna steaks, about 200 g (7 oz) each and 2.5 cm (1 in) thick
2 tbsp sesame seeds, white or mixed
2 cm piece fresh ginger, finely grated
steps: Boil the edamame in salted water for 4 to 5 minutes until tender, drain and keep warm.
Stir the soy sauce, rice vinegar, lime juice, ginger, chilli flakes and 1 teaspoon of the sesame oil together to make the dressing.
Pat the tuna dry, brush with the remaining sesame oil and press both sides into the sesame seeds.

Heat the neutral oil in a heavy frying pan over high heat until it shimmers. Sear the tuna for 60 to 90 seconds per side so the outside is golden and the centre stays pink; cook a minute longer per side if you prefer it medium.
Rest the tuna for 2 minutes, then slice thickly. Toss the edamame and cucumber with half the dressing and divide between two plates.
Fan the tuna over the top, spoon on the rest of the dressing and finish with spring onions. Each plate is about 500 kcal with 63 g protein.

title: Lean Beef and Broccoli Stir-fry
intro: Thin strips of lean sirloin tossed with crisp broccoli in a glossy garlic-ginger sauce, served over brown rice.
ingredients: 800 g (1¾ lb) lean beef sirloin, trimmed and sliced thinly against the grain
600 g (1 lb 5 oz) broccoli, cut into florets
120 ml (½ cup) beef stock or water
steps: Cook the brown rice in plenty of boiling water for 25 to 30 minutes until tender, then drain well and keep warm.
Toss the beef with 1 tablespoon of the soy sauce and the cornflour and leave for 10 minutes. Mix the remaining soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar and stock in a small bowl for the sauce.
Bring a pan of water to the boil and blanch the broccoli for 2 minutes until bright green; drain and rinse under cold water.
Heat a wok over the highest heat until smoking. Add half the oil and stir-fry half the beef for 1 to 2 minutes until just browned; remove and repeat with the remaining oil and beef.
Add the garlic and ginger to the wok for 20 seconds, then return the beef and add the broccoli and sauce. Toss for 1 to 2 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats everything.
Drizzle with sesame oil, scatter with spring onions and serve over the rice. Each serving is around 590 kcal with 52 g protein.

title: Cottage Cheese Protein Pancakes
intro: Tender, golden pancakes blended from cottage cheese, eggs and oats that taste like a treat and eat like a protein shake.
ingredients: 200 ml (¾ cup plus 1 tbsp) liquid egg whites
1 tsp butter or oil, for the pan
150 g (1 cup) fresh berries, to serve
steps: Put the cottage cheese, eggs, egg whites, oats, baking powder, vanilla, cinnamon and salt in a blender and blitz for 30 to 45 seconds until smooth. Let the batter rest for 5 minutes so the oats soften and it thickens slightly.
Heat a large non-stick frying pan over medium heat and lightly grease it with the butter or oil.
Pour in about 60 ml (¼ cup) of batter per pancake, cooking three at a time. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes until bubbles appear and the edges look set.
Flip carefully and cook for another 1 to 2 minutes until golden. Keep warm on a plate while you cook the rest; you should get about 10 pancakes.
Divide between two plates and top with the berries and Greek yogurt. Each stack provides around 500 kcal and 48 g protein.

title: Garlic Shrimp with Brown Rice
intro: Plump shrimp sizzled with garlic, chilli and lemon over nutty brown rice and wilted spinach.
ingredients: 500 g (1 lb 2 oz) raw peeled shrimp, tails removed
110 g (generous ½ cup) uncooked brown rice
steps: Cook the brown rice in a pan of boiling salted water for 25 to 30 minutes until tender, then drain and keep warm.
Pat the shrimp dry and season with salt, pepper and the paprika.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the garlic and chilli flakes and cook for 30 to 45 seconds until just golden and fragrant.
Add the shrimp in a single layer and cook for 1½ to 2 minutes per side until pink and opaque. Add the lemon zest and juice and toss for 30 seconds.
Push the shrimp to one side, add the spinach and toss for 1 minute until wilted. Stir in the parsley.
Serve the shrimp and spinach over the rice with the pan juices spooned on top. Each plate is about 540 kcal with 56 g protein.

title: Tofu and Tempeh Power Bowl
intro: Crisp baked tofu and pan-fried tempeh over edamame, kale and shredded vegetables with a punchy ginger-sesame dressing.
ingredients: 300 g (10½ oz) extra-firm tofu, pressed and cut into 2 cm cubes
240 g (8½ oz) tempeh, sliced 1 cm thick
2 cm piece fresh ginger, finely grated
100 g (3½ oz) kale, stems removed and leaves shredded
150 g (2 cups) red cabbage, finely shredded
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F, fan 180 °C) and line a tray with parchment. Toss the tofu cubes with 1 tablespoon of the soy sauce, then the cornflour, and spread them on the tray. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, turning halfway, until crisp and golden.
Whisk the remaining soy sauce with the sesame oil, rice vinegar, maple syrup, ginger and garlic to make the dressing.
Heat the vegetable oil in a frying pan over medium heat and cook the tempeh slices for 3 to 4 minutes per side until browned. Spoon over 1 tablespoon of the dressing and let it sizzle for 30 seconds.
Boil the edamame for 4 minutes, drain, and while hot toss with the kale and 1 tablespoon of dressing, scrunching the leaves with your hands to soften them.

Divide the kale and edamame, cabbage and carrot between two bowls. Top with the tofu and tempeh, pour over the remaining dressing and scatter with sesame seeds. Each bowl is about 560 kcal with 49 g protein.
